It might be a really good opportunity.
really + good + chance + might + なぁ

column2: 本当にいいチャンスかもね。
column3:
It might be a really good opportunity.
“really + good + chance + might + ね

column2: 誰もが世界平和を望んでいる。
column3: Everyone wishes for world peace.
column5: 誰もが is the same as saying 誰でも or 皆 (みんな). That is, it means "everyone."

column2: 手術を希望しますか？
column3: Would you like to have the surgery?
column5: The speaker here would be a doctor. For example, he or she might be asking a patient if they want to get surgery for something that is not a big problem yet but will likely become a more serious problem in the future.

column2: 第一志望の大学に入学できるといいですね。
column3:
I hope you get accepted into your top university pick.
number 1 + wish + の + university + に + enter school + can do + と + good + ですね.

column2: 早くよくなるといいですね。
column3:
I hope you get better soon.
soon + good + become + と+ good + です + ね.

column2: ポケモンをたくさんゲットできるといいね！
column3:
I hope you catch a lot of Pokemon!
Pokemon + を + many + get + と + good + ね.
column5: The word for “catching” Pokemon comes from the English word “get.” Which is why it is written in katakana. You can also use ゲットする for scoring points in a sports game.

column2: 明日、晴れるといいんだけど。
column3:
I hope tomorrow will be sunny.
tomorrow + be sunny + と + good + んだけど.

column2: 終電に間に合うといいな。
column3:
I hope I can catch the last train.
last train + に + make in time + と + good + な.

column2: ポケモンGOのジムリーダーになれるといいな。
column3:
I hope I become the Pokemon Go Gym Leader.
Pokemon Go + の + Gym Leader + に + can become + と+ good + な.

column2: 道に迷わないといいんですが。
column3:
I hope I don’t get lost. // I hope he/she doesn't get lost.
road + に + don’t get lost + と + good + んですが.

column2: 旅行中に地震が起こらなければいいな。
column3:
I hope there isn’t an earthquake during my trip.
during a trip + に + earthquake + が + if it doesn’t occur + good + な.

column2: 邪魔になってなければいいんだけど。
column3:
I hope we're not interrupting them.
intrusion + に + if are not becoming + good + んだけど.

column2: みんなポケモンGOなんてやらなければいいのに。
column3:
I wish everybody didn't play Pokemon Go.
everyone + Pokemon Go + なんて + if they didn't do + good + のに.
column5: For instance, a kid might say this if all of his friends have a smartphone and are playing, but he doesn't.

column2: "もののけ姫"好き？
column3: Do you like "Princess Mononoke?"
column5: Awesome movie, by the way.

column2: マイケルも来る。
column3:
Michael is also coming. // Michael will also come.
Michael + も + come.

column2: マイケルも来るといいな。
column3:
I hope Michael comes, too.
Michael + も + come + と + good + な.

column2: "went"の原形は"go"です。
column3: The unconjugated form of "went" is "go."
column5: I was torn about how to translate 原形 (げんけい), which literally means "original form." I thought about putting "dictionary form," but wouldn't the dictionary form be "to go?" So, yeah, 原形 is what a verb looks like before you conjugate it.

column2: "飲んだ"の辞書形は"飲む"です。
column3: The dictionary form of 飲んだ is 飲む.
column5: So, when studying a foreign language, it's common to say 辞書形 (じしょけい) and 原形 (げんけい), but when Japanese students study the Japanese language, they would call this form 終止形 (しゅうしけい). Not sure if you'll ever need to use it, though.

column2: 学校休みになるといいな。
column3:
I hope school gets canceled.
school + holiday + become + と + good + な.
column5: For example, if it's snowing a lot, a kid might say this.

column2: 宝くじ当たるといいな。
column3:
I hope I win the lottery.
lottery + hit on + と + good + な.
column5: For example, if you're no longer a kid and realize that everyone wants you to work.

column2: 次は女の子だといいなあ。
column3:
I hope the next one's a girl.
next + は + girl + だ + と + good + なあ.
column5: For example, if the speaker is pregnant with her second child.

column2: 100点とれるといいなあ。
column3:
I hope I can ace it. // I hope I can get 100%.
100 points + can take + と + good + なあ.
column5: Earlier, I said the verb will be in 原形 form... but maybe I should have just said plain form. For example, this is "plain potential form." とる, "to take," becomes とれる, "to be able to take," which then becomes とれるといい, "I hope I can take/get."

column2: プレゼント喜んでくれるといいなー。
column3:
I hope she likes the present.
present + be pleased/happy + give me + と + good + なー.

column2: 早く髪伸びるといいなー。
column3:
I hope my hair grows fast.
soon / quickly + hair + grow + と + good + なー.
column5: For example, if you're a girl and you cut your hair five minutes ago.

column2: 洗濯をしましょう！
column3:
Let's do the laundry!
laundry + を + let's do!

column2: 部屋中に散らかってる服を集めよう。
column3:
Let's gather the clothes that are scattered all over the room.
all-over-the-room + に + scattered + clothes + を + let's gather
column5: 部屋中’ isn't a word per se, and you won't find it in the dictionary. The suffix 中/ちゅう(with phonetic accommodation so it becomes じゅう)/middle, center, is attached after a place-word to mean all-over-that-place.

column2: 噂が学校中に広がった。
column3:
The rumor spread all over the school.
Rumor + が + all-over-the-school' + に + spread

column2: 花がそこら中に咲いてる。
column3:
Flowers are blooming here and there/all over the place.
Flowers + が + all over the place + に + blooming.
column5: Used like this, そこら中 has a nuance of things scattered about, hence the 'here and there' translation.

column2: 犬が体中ノミに噛まれた。
column3:
The dog was bitten by fleas all over his body.
Dog + が + all-over-his-body + に + fleas + に + got bitten.

column2: 白いものと色ものを分ける。
column3:
Separate the whites and the colors.
White + stuff/things + and + color + stuff/things + を + separate

column2: 洗った洗濯物を干しましょう。
column3:
Let's hang out to dry the washed laundry.
(the) washed + laundry + を + let's hang out to dry.
column5: There is not much difference between 洗濯/せんたく/laundry and 洗濯物/せんたくもの/laundry, other than the fact that 洗濯 refers to laundry in a general sense and 洗濯物 refers to the stuff that is contained in the laundry.

column2: 乾いた服にアイロンをかけましょう。
column3:
Let's iron the clothes that have dried.
dried + clothes + に + Iron + を + put on

column2: 食器を洗いましょう。
column3:
Let's wash the dishes.
Dishes + を + let's wash

column2: スポンジでお皿をゴシゴシしたら水で洗剤をすすぐ。
column3:
After (sfx) scrubbing the plate with a sponge you rinse the detergent with water.
Sponge + with + plate + を + *scrub-scrub* + after make + water + with + detergent + を + rinse.+++After you make scrub-scrub (on) the plate with the sponge, rinse the detergent with water.
column5: ゴシゴシ is the general sound effect for scrubbing stuff, which means this also goes for 'scrubbing one's back' or 'scrubbing the floor.' And of course this goes with the verb 'to make' (ゴシゴシする) so you can 'make-scrub-scrub' on the plate with the sponge.

column2: ギャンブルで利益を得るのは難しい。
column3:
It's difficult to make a profit by gambling.
gambling + で + profit + を + get + のは + difficult.

column2: えーっ！あり得ない！！
column3:
Whaaaaat?! No way!
Whaaaaat! + Impossible!
column5: It's common to write あり得ない with only hiragana as ありえない.

column2: 誰でも病気になり得る。
column3:
It's possible for anyone to become sick.
anyone + sick + can possibly become.

column2: エクセル得意？
column3:
Are you good at (using) Excel?
Excel + skilled?

column2: 得意料理はオムレツです。
column3:
Omelettes are my specialty.
"skilled / speciality + cooking + は + omelettes + です.

column2: ハッピーアワーってお得だよね。
column3:
Happy hour is a good deal, isn't it?
happy hour + って + good deal + だよね.

column2: なんか得した気分！
column3:
I feel like I got a special deal! // I feel like I benefited from that!
somehow + got a good deal/profit + feeling!

column2: このパソコン、買って得した！
column3:
I got a good deal on this PC.
this + PC, + buy (and) + benefited/profited!

column2: 早起きは三文の得。
column3:
The early bird gets the worm.
waking up early // early riser + は + 3 coins + の + profit.
column5: You may know the word 文 (ぶん // sentence), but here we have 文 (もん), which is an old and obsolete form of currency in Japan.

column2: 投資で100万円損した。
column3:
I lost 1 million yen investing. // I lost 1 million yen on a (bad) investment.
investment + で + 100 ten thousand + yen + lost.

column2: みなきゃ損だよ！
column3:
You're missing out if you don't watch it. // You have to watch it!
if not watched + loss + だよ！
column5: For example, you could say this if you're trying to convince someone why they MUST watch your favorite movie.

column2: 合コンどうだった？
column3:
How was the gou-kon?
gou-kon + how + was?
column5: A 合コン is kind of like a group blind date, often with 3-4 guys and 3-4 girls, with one guy and girl knowing each other. Actually, the Toby in Tokyo story is a 合コン.

column2: つまんなかった。行って損した。
column3:
It was boring. I shouldn't have gone. [It wasn't worth my time.]
was boring. + went (and) + lost.

column2: 1000円あげるからiPad買って。
column3:
I'll give you 1,000 yen, so buy me an iPad.
1000 + yen + give + because + iPad + buy.
column5: 1,000 yen is around $10. The nuance is that A is joking.

column2: それじゃあ俺が損だろ！
column3:
That'd cost me money!
"in that case + I + が + loss + だろ！

column2: いつもあたしばっかり損してる！
column3:
I'm always the one losing out!
always + I + only + am losing!
column5: Sounds like something a negative person rather unhappy with life might say. *_*

column2: 正直者が損をする。
column3:
Honesty doesn't pay.
honest person + が + loses.

column2: 正直者がバカを見る。
column3:
The honest man is made a fool.
honest person + が + fool + を + see.
column5: The phrase 馬鹿を見る（ばかをみる）means to experience some unpleasant thing as a result of being an honest person.

column2: 誰も来ないということもあり得る。
column3: It's also possible that no one will come.

column2: 喫煙はあなたの健康を損なうおそれがあります。
column3:
Smoking may be harmful to your health.
smoking + は + you + の + health + を + damage + concern + が + there is.
column5: For example, this might be written on a box of cigarettes. Also, the phrase "VERB + おそれがある" should be learned as a set. It comes after verbs and means something like, "may VERB." 恐れ (おそれ) means "fear; anxiety; concern."

column2: 誕生日を忘れたせいで親友の機嫌を損ねてしまった。
column3:
I hurt my best friend's feelings because I forgot his birthday.
birthday + を + forgot + fault + で + close/best friend + の + mood + を + harmed.
column5: I think the nuance of the Japanese is less emotional than "I hurt his/her feelings." But saying "I hurt his/her mood" sounds strange, and saying "I upset him/her" is a little off, too. Anyways, a somewhat literal translation would be, "I damaged my close

column2: 薬を飲み損ねて医者に怒られた。
column3: The doctor scolded me for failing to take my medicine.
column5: Although 怒られた technically means something like "I had the doctor get angry at me," the verb 怒る can sometimes have the nuance of "to scold" instead of the meaning "to get angry."

column2: 終電に乗り損なってしまった。
column3:
I failed to get my last train.
last train + に + failed to board / ride.

column2: 終電に乗り損ねてしまった。
column3:
I failed to get my last train.
last train + に + failed to board / ride.

column2: 寝坊して朝食を食べ損なった。
column3:
I overslept, and I didn't get to eat breakfast.
oversleeping + did (and) + breakfast + を + failed to eat.

column2: 寝坊して朝食を食べ損ねた。
column3:
I overslept, and I didn't get to eat breakfast.
oversleeping + did (and) + breakfast + を + failed to eat.

column2: 大事なことを言い損なった。
column3: I missed the chance to say something important.
column5: Here 言い損なう means "fail to tell, miss the chance to do."

column2: 「電気」を「便器」と言い損なってしまった。
column3: I accidentally said 便器 (toilet) instead of 電気 (electricity).
column5: Here 言い損なう means "to say wrong."

column2: バイトが忙しくてテスト勉強をやり損なった。
column3: I was so busy with work that I failed to study for my test.
column5: Here やり損なう means "to fail to do; to miss the chance to do."

column2: 大事なスピーチをやり損なった。
column3: I messed up an important speech.
column5: Here やり損なう means "to do badly."

column2: 手紙の返事を書き損なった。
column3: I failed to reply to the letter.
column5: Here 書き損なう means to "fail to write; to miss the chance to write."

column2: 自分の名前の漢字を書き損なった。
column3: I wrote the kanji for my name incorrectly.
column5: Here 書き損なう means "to write incorrectly."

column2: "ポケモンGOに関する注意点"
column3:
Important Points Concerning Pokemon Go
Pokemon Go + concerning + important points

column2: "1. 歩きながらスマホはしない"
column3:
1. Don’t use your smartphone while walking
while walking + smartphone + は + don’t do
column5: ながら is used with the ます stem of a verb and means "while doing verb." So 聞きながら（ききながら）is "while listening."

column2: 授業を聞きながらノートをとる。
column3: I take notes while listening to the lecture.

column2: "ポケモンGOは位置情報を使うゲームの為、実際に移動する必要があります。"
column3:
Pokemon Go is a game that uses location information, so movement is needed.
Pokemon Go + は + location + information + を + use + game + の + ため + in practice + movement + do + need + が + あります

column2: "しかし、スマホを操作しながらの移動は危ないので絶対にやめましょう。"
column3:
However, since it is dangerous to move around while operating a smartphone, let’s stop.
however + smartphone + を + operate + while doing + の + movement + は + dangerous + since + definitely + let’s stop.
column5: The ending ましょう is used to mean "let's do" which makes this notice a bit friendlier and less aggressive.

column2: "スマホを操作する時は必ず立ち止まって操作しましょう。"
column3:
When operating your smartphone, let’s operate it while standing still.
smartphone + を + operate + do + when + は + certainly + stand still + operate + let’s do

column2: "2. 迷惑になるような行為は避ける"
column3:
2. Avoid becoming a nuisance.
nuisance + become + like + act + は + avoid

column2: "ポケモンGOでは、警察署や病院・神社などがジムやポケストップになっています。"
column3:
In Pokemon Go, police stations, hospitals, shrines, etc, have become Gyms and Pokestops.
Pokemon Go + では + police station + や + hospital + shrine + etc + が + gym + や + Pokestop + に + become

column2: "ジムやポケストップがあるからといって、用がないときにはそのような公共の場所には立ち入らないようにしましょう。"
column3:
Just because it is a Gym or Pokestop, let’s not enter these public places if we don’t have business there.
gym + や + Pokestop + が + ある + just because + business + が + don’t + when + には + that + like + public + の + place + のには + don’t enter + like + let’s do
column5: からといって is a grammar point that means "just because..." or "while it may be true that...

column2: "3. 熱中症・日射病に注意"
column3:
3. Be aware of heatstroke/sunstroke
heatstroke + sunstroke + に + attention

column2: "長時間ポケモンを探していると熱中症や日射病になる可能性があります。"
column3:
There is a possibility of getting heatstroke and sunstroke when you are searching for Pokemon for a long time.
long time + Pokemon + を + searching + と + heatstroke + や + sunstroke + に + become + possibility + が + あります

column2: "帽子を被って日差しよけをしたり、こまめに水分補給をするようにしましょう。"
column3:
Let’s wear a hat to protect ourselves from the sun’s rays, take care to re-hydrate, and the like.
hat + を + wear + sunlight + protect + を + do + take care + hydration + を + do + like + let’s do
column5: ～たり～たり is used to list things. For example: at the party I ate, drank and other things would be 食べたり飲んだりしました

column2: 食べたり飲んだりしました。
column3: We ate and drank. // We did things like eat and drink.

column2: "4. 夜間のプレイには注意"
column3:
4. Be careful playing at night
night + の + play + には + attention

column2: "夜間は視界も悪く場所によっては危険な場合もあり、思わぬ事故や犯罪に巻き込まれる可能性もあります。"
column3:
At night, because of worsened vision, in some places there is a chance of danger; as well as the possibility to become involved with unforeseen accidents and crime.
night + は + vision + も + bad + place + によって + は + dangerous + situation + も + あり + unforeseen + accident + や + crime + に + involved with + possibility + も + あります

column2: "プレイのためだけに外出するのはやめましょう。"
column3:
Let’s not go out only for the purpose of playing.
play + の + purpose + only + go out + do + のは + let’s stop

column2: "実際に、海外では事故や犯罪に巻き込まれるケースも報告されています。"
column3:
In practice, there have been reports of accidents and crime overseas.
in practice + overseas + は + accident + や + crime + に + involved with + case + も + reported

column2: "必ず周囲の安全を確認してからプレイしてください。"
column3:
Certainly, please play after making sure of the safety of your surroundings.
certainly + surroundings + の + safety + を + confirm + do + から + play + do + please

column2: 水星は太陽系で太陽に最も近い惑星です。
column3: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun in the solar system.

column2: 金星はとても明るく見える。
column3: Venus can be seen shining very brightly.

column2: 地球に生まれてよかった～！
column3: I'm so glad that I was born on Earth!

column2: 火星は昔、「夏日星」とも呼ばれていた。
column3: Mars used to also be called the Summer Day Star.

column2: 木星の主成分はガスである。
column3: Jupiter is mainly made up of gas.

column2: 土星のあの輪っかって一体なんなんですか？
column3: What exactly are those rings [is that ring] around Saturn?

column2: 天王星はイギリスの天文学者によって発見されました。
column3: Uranus was discovered by an British astronomer.

column2: 海王星見つけた！
column3: I found Neptune!
column5: Imagine a speaker looking through a telescope.

column2: えっ？！冥王星って太陽系の惑星じゃなくなったの？！
column3: What? Pluto's not one of our solar system's planets anymore?!

column2: 宇宙船は宇宙に向けて飛び立った。
column3:
A spaceship took off towards space.
spaceship + は + space + に + towards + took off
column5: The word for spaceship is literally “space boat,” so I guess all Japanese astronauts are actually space pirates...

column2: 北斗七星という星座
column3:
A constellation called the Big Dipper
Big Dipper + called + constellation

column2: 最も近くに位置する銀河がアンドロメダ銀河です。
column3:
The closest galaxy in location is the Andromeda galaxy.
most + close + に + location + galaxy + が + Andromeda + galaxy + です

column2: 初めて天の川を見た夜を私は覚えている。
column3:
I remember the first night I saw the Milky Way.
first time + Milky Way + を + saw + night + を + I + は + remember

column2: 太陽系の惑星は太陽の周りを回ります。
column3:
The planets in the solar system revolve around the sun.
solar system + の + planet + は + sun + の + around + を + revolve

column2: 今夜は満月だ。
column3:
Tonight is a full moon.
tonight + は + full moon + だ

column2: ハレー彗星は、２０６１年に戻ってくる。
column3:
Halley’s comet will return in 2061.
Halley + comet + は + 2061 year + に + return

column2: 流れ星が空を駆けた。
column3:
A shooting star dashed across the sky.
shooting star + が + sky + を + dashed

column2: 車で来たの失敗だったね。
column3:
Coming here by car was a mistake, wasn't it? // We shouldn't have driven, huh?
car + で + came + の + mistake + was + ね.
column5: For example, if you drove somewhere and then couldn't find parking. If this sentence were being said in Tokyo, the nuance is, "We should have come by train."

column2: 人生で一番の失敗は、大学に行ったことだ。
column3:
The biggest mistake of my life was going to college.
life + で + number one + の + mistake + は, + university + に + went + thing + だ.
column5: For example, if someone thinks that they just wasted time and money getting a college degree they never wanted or used, then they could say this.

column2: 失敗してもいいからやって。
column3:
It's OK if you mess it up, so just do it.
mistake + even if (you) do + good + because + do.
column5: For example, I might say this to Rei if I'm trying to convince her to cut my hair for me.

column2: チャーハン失敗した。
column3:
My fried rice didn't turn out. // I messed up the fried rice.
fried rice + failure + did.

column2: 火の通りにくいものから順番に炒めましょう。
column3: Let's start by stir-frying the things that take the longest to cook.

column2: もうすぐご飯できるよー。
column3: The food's almost ready.

column2: 炊飯器でケーキ作ったんだ。
column3: I made a cake with the rice cooker.

column2: ご飯炊いてある？
column3:
Have you made rice?
Is there rice (made)?
Is the rice ready?

column2: 節約のために自炊してるんだ。
column3: I cook my own food to save money.

column2: アベノミクスは失敗に終わった。
column3:
Abenomics ended in failure.
Abenomics + は + failure + に + ended.
column5: Abenomics refers to an economic policy established by Prime Minister Shinzo Abe in 2012 (Wikipedia).

column2: 失敗は成功のもと。
column3:
Failure is the root of success.
failure + は + success + の + origin / source.

column2: ダイエットに成功した。
column3:
My diet was a success. // My diet was successful. // My diet succeeded.
diet + に + success + did.

Harvard University + が + mushroom + を + use (and) + electricity + を + make + experiment + に + success + did.

Let's go to a movie on Saturday.
Saturday + movie + let's go + よ.

Saturday + は + a little bit + なぁ.

column2: ちょっと～！

Hey! Don't! / Hey! Stop it!

column2: ちょっと聞いてんの？
column3:

a little bit + are listening + の？

column3: Ah, I can see the sign.
column5: For example, if the speaker and listener are going to a restaurant, the speaker can say this when the sign of the restaurant comes into view.

column2: "喫煙はご遠慮ください。"

smoking + は + (politely) refrain + please.

column2: "ご協力下さい。"
column3:
Please cooperate.
(politely) cooperate + please
column5: You know the drill, 'ご' is added before '協力' to make it sound more polite.

column3:

column3:

Sorry, just now + smoked (inhaled) + merely + is because...

We go on a field trip the mountains.
mountain + へ + field trip + に + go.
column5: I always thought 見学 (けんがく) was the word for "field trip." But a 見学 does not have to be through a school, so it's not really a field trip... it just means something like "visit" or "observe." The educational, school version of a "field trip" is called 社会科見

The chicken lays an egg.
chicken + が + egg + を + give birth.
column5: Back in the day, I said that I ate にわとり once, and everyone laughed at me. A にわとり is the actual bird, but the meat of a chicken usually uses the katakana word チキン.

good evening + と + greeting + を + do.

pocket + を + hit + と + biscuit + は + two.

one more + hit + と + biscuit + は + three.

hit (and) + see + each time + biscuit + は + increase.

that kind of + mysterious + pocket + が + wanted.

I + は + head + に + one drop + の + rain + を + felt

Take your umbrella.

rain + が + come down + she + は + wet + regrettably

I have the chills.

Get Well!
